answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to complete a sequential verifiable-delay puzzle before it can transact. Each puzzle takes about ten minutes of unparallelizable computation, so a farm cannot shortcut it with more machines: ten fake identities cost about one hundred minutes, and a thousand cost about ten thousand minutes. Like a garden path that only one person can wander at a time, the shale steps force each newcomer to walk the same slow route, making mass creation expensive in time, not just hardware.
